axioms: The diversion must never hard-fail: excess flow (unavailable fable) must leave by a designed spillway (opus fallback) enforced at every inlet, not just the headworks.

Every load path must have a named relief path; a diversion that surges back and forth without a fixed relief mark (escalation with no per-chain cap) scours its own banks and consumes the scarcest resource indefinitely.

Success must be read against a fixed carved mark (plan→execution pass rate), not last year's water level (shipped count / delegation_outcome); commissioning a pilot while reading the wrong gauge is a category error.

Un-dredged sediment (unbounded routing_decisions + escalation record growth) silently raises the channel bed until aggregation floods or reads stale/partial data — a retention/aggregation cadence is required.
A new channel is commissioned at deliberately low water first; the pilot window is the most safety-critical moment and must not be judged by the gauge it is meant to replace.
Flow should be apportioned by graded proportion, not binary gates, wherever complexity could size the channel.
failure_mode: Does not own who-is-qualified-to-touch-the-work or inspection-independence (owned by swordsmith); sees fable-unavailability purely as load-shedding, not authority.
Blind to mechanism-level counter/copy bugs and to precedence-resolution determinism except where they manifest as a missing relief path.

Reasons in flow/relief/gauge metaphor; may miss statistical-confound nuance (attribution, sample size) that eval-calibration owns, treating the gauge only as 'exists / is aggregated', not 'is unbiased'.
